handbookNote: Maryland Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Maryland previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only md_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Maryland Real Estate Commission (MREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly reading PSI's own official 'State of Maryland Real Estate Commission Candidate Information Bulletin and Application Forms' (bulletin id 529, copyright PSI Services LLC 2024, updated 8/15/2024). Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker exam = National portion 75 items (80 points possible -- a footnote states 'National broker exams include questions that are scored up to two points', disclosed here rather than silently flattened), 90 minutes; State portion 40 items (40 points), 30 minutes; combined 115 items (120 points), 120-minute time limit. Passing, quoted directly from the bulletin's own Score Reporting table (Broker row): National Portion 56 (of 80 points), State Portion 28 (of 40) -- both portions independently scored and both must be passed; 84 of 120 combined points = exactly 70%. This site's track_registry schema models one combined row rather than two separately-scored portions, so the DB row records combined totals (115 questions, 7200s/120min duration, 70% pass, min_correct=81 as the nearest whole-item rounding of 115 x 0.70=80.5) -- matching New Jersey's and Massachusetts's own resolved 115-item/70%-pass/min_correct-81 structure exactly (see nj_re_broker.json, ma_re_broker.json), though Maryland's real combined time limit is notably shorter at 120 minutes vs. NJ/MA's 240 minutes. A small number of 1-10 unscored experimental items (~10% of the exam) may also appear, counted against exam time. CONTENT OUTLINE -- National portion percentages, quoted verbatim from the bulletin (Broker column, summing to exactly 100% of the 75-item national portion, independently re-verified by hand this session): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single national topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (Broker-only sub-items on maintenance/improvements/reporting/risk management and trust-fund handling), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (Broker-only Supervisory Responsibilities sub-section), Real Estate Calculations 6%. NOTABLE: these percentages are IDENTICAL to every other PSI-administered state in this campaign (NJ/TN/VA/AZ/MA/MO/MN/SC) -- yet further confirmation PSI uses one shared multi-state 'National Portion' content-outline template for real estate broker exams nationwide. Maryland State Portion, quoted verbatim as item counts (of the 40-item state portion, Broker column, summing to the full 40): Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission 5 items (General Powers; Investigations, Hearings, and Appeals; Suspensions, Revocations, and Penalties; Guaranty Fund; Examination of Records -- Broker Only); Licensing Requirements 8 items (Activities Requiring a License; Change in License Status; License Renewals; Continuing Education Requirements; Partnerships and Corporations; Place of Business; Percentage of Ownership for Businesses); Brokerage Relationships 7 items (Listing Agreements; Disclosure of Brokerage Relationship; Disclosure of Interest in Property/Conflict of Interest Disclosures); Supervision 6 items (Handling Monies including Trust Monies; Recordkeeping Requirements including electronic recordkeeping; Supervision Requirements; Knowledge of Other Maryland State Laws -- short sale, home improvements, PIFHA); Business Conduct 9 items (Offers; Commissions including rebates; Advertising and Signs; Fair Housing Laws and Regulations; Summary Suspensions/Convictions); Ethics 5 items (Unfair Inducements; Dealings with Other Licensees; General Ethics). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights, not an even split -- actual per-bucket counts were then set by each drafting pass to whatever its real, verifiable source material actually supported, with NO target number or ceiling given to any drafting pass -- the corrected drafting methodology adopted after discovering and fixing a target-anchoring bug earlier in this campaign (see mo_re_broker.json for the full incident writeup); this bank was drafted fresh under the corrected policy from the start, not backfilled after the fact. Real Maryland statute/regulation facts grounded in the Annotated Code of Maryland, Real Property Article, Title 17 (Real Estate Brokers) and the Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR) Title 09, Subtitle 11 (State Real Estate Commission) -- both of which this project has prior primary-source working copies of on disk from an earlier research pass (title17_statute_clean.txt and comar_09_11_final.txt), including specific provisions such as the Guaranty Fund (Real Property Article Sec. 17-404 et seq., compensating the public for licensee fraud/misrepresentation/conversion up to a statutory per-claim cap), the Commission's investigation/hearing/appeal authority and disciplinary sanctions (Sec. 17-322 et seq.), trust/escrow money handling and recordkeeping requirements (COMAR 09.11.01 and 09.11.02), broker supervision requirements over associate licensees, branch office and place-of-business rules, continuing education requirements, and Maryland's real consumer-protection statutes referenced in the bulletin's own outline -- Maryland's short sale disclosure requirements, Home Improvement Law framework, and the Protection of Homeowners in Foreclosure Act (PIFHA), which the bulletin explicitly names as required 'Knowledge of Other Maryland State Laws' content under the Supervision topic. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a Maryland-specific statute is sourced to 'national real estate practice principles' framing throughout. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate. This bank was drafted across 17 parallel single-topic drafting passes (11 national + 6 Maryland state-law categories), each pass instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. A cross-bucket source_note-citation dedup check across all 17 files found ZERO cross-bucket near-duplicates, matching Minnesota's clean result earlier in this campaign. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_md_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 17 bucket files combined, in file order), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.0/25.0/25.0% A/B/C/D distribution. 609 raw questions drafted against a 115-item exam -- a 5.30:1 pool ratio, comfortably clearing both the standing 4:1 new-track floor and the 5:1 project-wide aspiration with no backfill pass needed.
